title: Validation of Flood Inundation Distribution in the Boro Watershed Using Sentinel-1 Imagery and 1D HEC-RAS Simulation Against Field Observation Data

idea.research_question: Can Sentinel-1 backscatter change reliably delineate flood inundation in the Boro watershed?
idea.hypothesis: Flood-event Sentinel-1 backscatter changes relative to comparable pre-event observations identify inundated areas more accurately than a static water baseline.
idea.mechanism: Align pre-event and event Sentinel-1 scenes by acquisition geometry, calculate polarization-specific change metrics, and classify persistent flood signals after masking confounding water and unsuitable terrain.
idea.analytical_approach: Single-source Sentinel-1 SAR flood-inundation mapping with event-window sensitivity and independent validation where available
idea.expected_contribution: A reproducible single-dataset benchmark for Sentinel-1 flood-inundation detection without requiring local HEC-RAS model outputs.
idea.falsification_condition: Reject the hypothesis if event-to-baseline backscatter changes do not improve flood delineation over a permanent-water or no-change baseline.

seed_audit.migration_note: Migrated from dual_dataset/task_031 on 2026-10-07; the local 1D HEC-RAS output is unavailable, so the active contract retains only public Sentinel-1 observations.
